Interface TypeHierarchy

All Known Implementing Classes:
GeneratedTypeHierarchy
public sealed interface TypeHierarchy permits GeneratedTypeHierarchy
The generic hierarchy of a type as it was declared: its type variables with their bounds, its generic superclass and generic interfaces, and every super type it has, transitively, with their type arguments written in terms of those variables.

A hierarchy is recorded at compile time, by the Micronaut processors, for the types a compilation asks for with TypeHierarchyImport or through VisitorContext.importTypeHierarchy(ClassElement, Element...), and found at run time with TypeHierarchies.find(Class). It is read from the record only: no signature of the class is read reflectively. Unlike a bean definition or a bean introspection, a hierarchy can be recorded for any class a compilation sees, a class of a library or of the JDK included, and describes nothing but the declaration of the type.

The super types are the ones ClassElement.getAllSuperTypes() lists at compile time, so the hierarchy is walked once, by the compiler: the super class before the interfaces, each followed by its own super types in declaration order, a type reached twice listed once, Object last. The arguments keep what the declaration says: a type variable is a GenericPlaceholder with its bounds, a wildcard is a WildcardArgument, a type used without its type arguments is a raw type (Argument.isRawType()) and so are its super types, and an array of a variable is a placeholder whose type is the array of the erasure of the variable. getTypeClosure(Argument) substitutes the actual arguments of a parameterization into each entry.

Since:
5.3.0
Author:
Denis Stepanov

    • getTypeClosure

      default List<Argument<?>> getTypeClosure(Argument<?> parameterization)
      The type closure of a parameterization of the type: the parameterization itself, then each of the super types with the actual type arguments substituted for the type variables, in the same order, Object last.

      The substitution follows the Java Language Specification. A type variable is replaced by the actual type argument at its position, an array of a variable by an array of that argument, and a wildcard argument is kept as a wildcard. A raw parameterization of a generic type, one with no type arguments or marked raw, erases every super type (JLS 4.8). A variable the record does not declare is kept as it is. The annotations written on a type use in the declaration, extends @A Base<@B T>, are those of the entries, and a substituted variable carries the annotations of its use unless the actual argument has annotations of its own.

      Parameters:
      parameterization - The type with its type arguments, or raw
      Returns:
      The closure
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if the parameterization is not of the type
